title: Tam Pà Ling cave, Laos
summary: Tam Pà Ling, a cave in northern Laos, holds some of the earliest fossil evidence of Homo sapiens in mainland Southeast Asia. Fossils were washed in over many millennia; a frontal bone dates to about 70,000 years ago and a tibia to about 77,000, hinting at an early dispersal that may have left no descendants.

uncertainty.note: The Flinders summary says fossils were deposited between about 86,000 and 30,000 years ago; dated human remains span 77 ± 9 kyr (tibia), 70 ± 3 kyr (frontal) and 52–40 kyr (skull and mandible). Years before present, not calibrated to 1950.

when.display: c. 86,000–30,000 years ago (oldest dated human remains c. 77,000–70,000 years ago)

where.modern_name: Tam Pà Ling cave, northern Laos
where.historical_name: Tam Pà Ling cave, upland northern Laos; no polity

importance.justification: Among the oldest dated Homo sapiens fossils on the Southeast Asian mainland.

sources.title: Tam Pà Ling hominin fossils (Nature Communications, 2023)
